images.title: Split one piece in two
images.purpose: Set up the question: from a circle filled exactly by 1/2, 1/3 and 1/6, split one piece into two different smaller fractional units to make four different units that total 1.
images.composition: One large circle on the left with wide space around it, and a short column of text lines on the right.
images.exact_structure: One large flat circle, the whole, with a dark outline, filled with no gaps by three sectors: one teal #0072B2 sector of exactly one half (180 degrees), one amber #E69F00 sector of exactly one third (120 degrees), and one sector of exactly one sixth (60 degrees) filled reddish purple #CC79A7. One grey #6B7280 dashed line from the centre crosses the purple sector, splitting it into two unequal parts, neither part labelled. Right: two short text lines stacked with wide spacing. Exactly 1 circle, 3 sectors, 1 dashed line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any fraction written on either part of the split sixth, or any finished set of four units shown
images.takeaway: Split one unit into two different smaller units.
images.description: A circle filled exactly by a teal half, an amber third and a purple sixth, with a dashed line showing the sixth is to be split into two different units. No finished set of four units is shown.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the purple piece and say which two different units could add up to it.

image_decisions.why: A filled circle with one piece ready to split shows the method cue without giving any of the six solutions.
